payload.chart:
MORPHOLOGICAL CHART over the partitioned clusters. Options fed by the state-of-the-art scan for architectures, run at the owner's explicit instruction ('do some prior art research when you make your decision - if you find something better, use that'), so the chart lists what exists rather than what I assumed.

ROW 1 - WORKING-TREE SEARCH (K1/F1)
(a) hand-rolled literal/ranked/fuzzy - TODAY. (b) ripgrep via @vscode/ripgrep. (c) system ripgrep on PATH. (d) ast-grep (AST patterns). (e) trigram index server - zoekt / Sourcegraph / OpenGrok. (f) semantic / embedding retrieval.
PRUNED: (c) - PROBED FALSE, rg is not on PATH on the owner's own machine (run-6405dc1414a2); relying on it would make install luck. (e) - violates C1 FRESHNESS as a veto: these are index servers, and Sourcegraph indexes the default branch with other branches as opt-in; also a server contradicts C3 one-click install for a single-user system. (f) - violates C1 for the same reason and was already rejected at frame_delta. (d) - KEPT but only as an ADDITION, never as a replacement: it answers structural questions our exact search cannot, and nothing in the register asks a structural question yet.

ROW 2 - RECORD SEARCH ACROSS REFS (K1/F4)
(a) git grep over refs - PROBED PASS, returns ref:path:count. (b) check out a ref, then search the checkout. (c) index the refs (zoekt). (d) none.
PRUNED: (b) - a checkout per query is slow, mutates the working tree and cannot run while an iteration is open; it also fails C1's spirit by making the answer depend on what is currently checked out. (c) - as row 1(e). (d) - fails C2 REACH as a veto: killer story S1 dies.

ROW 3 - READING A FILE (K1/F2)
(a) whole file only - TODAY, and the reason the design document is unreadable. (b) offset/limit range with total reported. (c) extract ranges via the search tool.
PRUNED: (c) - makes reading depend on the search dependency for no gain, and couples two clusters that the DSM keeps apart.

ROW 4 - LOCATING FILES BY NAME (K1/F1)
(a) directory walk - TODAY. (b) rg --files with globs. (c) git ls-files with pathspecs. (d) a glob npm package.
PRUNED: (d) - a third dependency for something (b) and (c) each already give free. Note (c) sees only TRACKED files, which matters for untracked work-in-progress.

ROW 5 - MANY EDITS (K3/F10)
(a) one edit per call - TODAY. (b) an ops array applied atomically. (c) generate and apply a patch file.
PRUNED: (c) - patch application is fuzzy by nature and would weaken the per-edit CAS guard that R12 requires.

ROW 6 - SELECTING THE RULES THAT BIND A STATE (K4/F14) - THE HARD ROW, because P5 proved the obvious option does not exist
(a) hand-written guidance per state - TODAY; the thing being replaced. (b) machine-readable applies_to selectors (state ids / kinds / tags) plus a migration of the ten existing nodes. (c) semantic match: reuse the existing BM25 index over applies_to text against the state's statement. (d) each state DECLARES the rules it carries. (e) hybrid - selectors where present, semantic as a widener.
PRUNED: (d) - it is exactly the hand-wiring whose absence caused the problem; a law minted tomorrow would still need every state edited. Rejected on sight and recorded so the rejection is visible.
KEPT AND GENUINELY CONTESTED: (b), (c), (e). (b) is checkable but needs authoring discipline forever; (c) needs no migration but is fuzzy exactly where C7 SELECTION CORRECTNESS is decisive; (e) may inherit both virtues or both vices.

ROW 7 - WHERE LINTS LIVE (K5/F17-F18)
(a) inline in each gate handler. (b) a registry keyed by check id, declared on the machine-state node. (c) an external script per lint.
PRUNED: (a) - scatters the checks and guarantees drift from the guidance that describes them, breaking the K4-K5 contract edge the DSM names as load-bearing. (c) - re-creates the untested-duplicate problem and puts checks outside the ledger's reach.

ROW 8 - HOW A VERDICT IS RECORDED (K5/F21)
(a) inside the evidence field, mixed with prose. (b) a separate verdict block in the evidence and the grant. (c) both.
PRUNED: (a) - fails R20 outright: if the verdict is prose among prose, computed and asserted are not distinguishable without reading, which is the audit the owner needs.

ROW 9 - NAMING THE RECORD (K6/F22-F24)
(a) lightweight tag only - TODAY. (b) annotated tag plus the commit hash in the grant. (c) commit hash only. (d) (b) plus deleting the iteration branch.
PRUNED: (a) - PROBED DEFECTIVE: push.followTags drops lightweight tags, and git already warns the branch/tag name is ambiguous. (c) - loses the readable name a person can type, which F23 exists for.

ROW 10 - MACHINE-LOCAL CONFIG (K6/F26-F27)
(a) none - TODAY. (b) a dedicated se_config tool. (c) extend se_file_* with a config root.
PRUNED: (c) - it would make the file lane a writer outside the product, breaking draw_context's boundary for a convenience.
payload.shortlist:
THREE CANDIDATES seeded for parallel elaboration. The datum at converge_pugh is TODAY (the shipped surface), and one candidate exists specifically to test whether the dependency is needed at all.

X1 'RIPGREP + GIT, SELECTORS' - 1b, 2a, 3b, 4b, 5b, 6b, 7b, 8b, 9d, 10b. Ripgrep for the tree via the npm package, git grep for refs, range reads, rg --files for globs, atomic ops batching, machine-readable applies_to selectors with a ten-node migration, a lint registry declared on state nodes, verdicts in their own block, annotated tag plus hash plus branch deletion, se_config. The straightforward reading of the kickoff.

X2 'RIPGREP + GIT, SEMANTIC JOIN' - identical to X1 except row 6 takes (c): reuse the existing BM25 index to match a state against applies_to prose. Exists because P5 showed applies_to is prose today, and because we already own a working semantic index for exactly this kind of text. Its risk is precisely C7: it may pull in plausible-but-wrong rules, which costs attention while looking like coverage.

X3 'GIT ONLY, NO NEW DEPENDENCY' - 1(git grep), 2a, 3b, 4c, 5b, 6b, 7b, 8b, 9d, 10b. THE HONEST ALTERNATIVE, and it deserves elaboration rather than dismissal: git grep searches the WORKING TREE as well as refs, supports -n, -C context, -l, -c and pathspec globs, and git ls-files covers file listing. That would satisfy C2 REACH and C5 ONE IMPLEMENTATION with ZERO new dependencies and one code path for both tree and record - arguably a better answer to the owner's own 'no duplicate code' ruling than adding rg beside git. What it sheds: no --json (text output must be parsed), no multiline, no type filters, and it sees only TRACKED files by default - untracked work-in-progress becomes invisible unless asked for. Whether those losses matter is what the matrix must decide, not my prior.

NOT SEEDED, with reasons: any candidate using an index server or embeddings (killed by the C1 freshness veto before scoring); any candidate keeping the hand-rolled searcher beside a new one (killed by C5 and by the owner's explicit ruling); ast-grep as a REPLACEMENT (it answers a question nothing in the register asks) - though it is recorded as a clean later ADDITION with its trigger, per the escalation model the field scan found.
